title: S-TiUltra Implant Study
official: Comparison of Early Healing Dynamics Between Nobel Biocare TiUnite and the Novel S TiUltra Implants Using Resonance Frequency Analysis: A Prospective Clinical Study
summary: This prospective clinical study will compare early healing and implant stability between two Nobel Biocare dental implant systems, NobelReplace S-TiUltra and NobelReplace CC TiUnite. Approximately 30 implants will be randomly assigned to one of the two implant groups and followed for 12 weeks after placement. Implant stability will be assessed using resonance frequency analysis at implant placement and at approximately 2, 4, 6, 8, and 12 weeks. Clinical healing, radiographic findings, and other treatment-related outcomes will also be evaluated during the follow-up period.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age ≥18 years
* Male or Female
* Partially edentulous patients
* Healed ridges (≥3 months post-extraction with no history of socket preservation or ridge augmentation)
* Adequate bone volume (no need for major grafting)
* Sites requiring a single unit implant
* Provision of informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Systemic or local disease or condition that would compromise bone metabolism, post-operative healing and/or osseointegration e.g. uncontrolled diabetes with self-reported most recent HbA1C \> 8.0 within last six months
* Systemic corticosteroids or any other medication that would influence bone metabolism, post-operative healing, and/or osseointegration
* History of osseous degenerative diseases
* Heavy smoking (\>10 cigarettes/day)
* Bisphosphonate/antiresorptive therapy
* uncontrolled periodontal disease
* Irradiated bone
* Previous history of failed implants
* Recently grafted/augmented site (\< 1 year)
